served.bankWhy: Paragraph 11 links two facts: MAC is built on movement, and the relaxant removes movement. With the sign gone, the standard measure has nothing left to read.

passage.title: Why Anaesthesia Still Lacks an Explanation

distractorNotes: The passage says nothing about relaxants changing how much agent is required.
Amnesia is credited to the anaesthetic at low doses, not to the relaxant.
Each drug in the bundle keeps its own job, and the opioid's job is the reflex response to injury.
The monitors described next read the brain's electrical signal, which paralysis does not silence.

answer.text: the sign that the standard measure of depth depends on can no longer be seen
answer.line: The relaxant removes movement, and movement is the sign the standard measure of depth, MAC, was built on.

steps: Find the relaxant: paragraph 11, sentence 2. It "removes the very sign, movement, on which the standard measure of depth was built".
Chase "standard measure" back to paragraph 9. MAC is defined by whether patients move when the skin is cut.
Join the two. A paralyzed patient cannot move, so the measure has nothing left to read.

choices.text: the sign that the standard measure of depth depends on can no longer be seen
choices.note: Movement is the sign, the relaxant takes it away, and the measure is left with nothing to read.

choices.text: muscle relaxants lower the concentration of agent that a patient turns out to need
choices.note: No line says a relaxant changes how much agent a patient needs.

choices.text: relaxants are known to erase the memory of the procedure
choices.note: Memory loss is tied to the non-immobilizers in paragraph 5 and to low doses of agent in paragraph 10, never to relaxants.

choices.text: the opioid in the mixture becomes unnecessary once movement has stopped
choices.note: Sentence 1 gives the opioid its own job, the reflex responses to injury. Nothing says stillness makes it unnecessary.

choices.text: paralysis makes the electroencephalogram impossible to record
choices.note: Paragraph 12 has monitors reading the electroencephalogram from forehead electrodes. The passage never says paralysis stops the recording.
